terms.definition: A virus that causes a mosaic pattern of discolouration on leaves, reducing photosynthesis and growth.
terms.examiner: A plant disease caused by a virus.

terms.definition: A fungal disease: purple or black spots on leaves, which turn yellow and drop early, reducing photosynthesis.
terms.examiner: Spread in water or by wind; treated with fungicides and removing affected leaves.

terms.definition: Insects that feed on phloem sap; an example of an insect pest.
terms.examiner: Pests are controlled by insecticides or by predators such as ladybirds.

terms.definition: Lack of nitrate ions causes stunted growth, because nitrates are needed to make proteins.
terms.examiner: Nitrates are taken up by active transport.

terms.definition: Lack of magnesium causes chlorosis (yellow leaves), because magnesium is needed for chlorophyll.
Cellulose cell walls, a tough waxy cuticle and layers of dead cells (bark) that stop pathogens entering.
terms.examiner: Contrast with chemical and mechanical defences.

terms.definition: Antibacterial chemicals and poisons that deter herbivores.
terms.examiner: Mint and witch hazel make antibacterial chemicals.

terms.definition: Thorns and hairs, leaves that droop or curl when touched, and mimicry to trick animals.
terms.examiner: Mechanical adaptations deter animals from touching or eating the plant.
